text.p: - Slovenian Foreign Minister Davorin Kracun met representatives of several U.S. companies during his visit to New York this week.
- The police said they have not yet found the person who put a bomb in front of a Slovenian judge's home earlier this week, seriously injuring the judge's wife.

- Parliament still has to determine the voting procedure of the electoral referendum set for December 8, when Slovenians will have to decide on one of three proposals for a change of electoral system.
- A parliamentary committee investigating the bankruptcy of most parts of former electonic giant Iskra in the early 1990's said it would soon prepare its final report.
- In the first eight months of 1996 income from tourism in Slovenia was $0.75 billion and should reach about $1.1 billion by the end of the year, tourism officials said.
- The Ljubljana city council raised rents for business premises in the capital by 50 percent.
- A two-day Internet fair to present the Internet to the Slovenian public started in Ljubljana on Thursday.

- Slovenian investment companies have pushed the government to determine additional companies that would take part in a general voucher privatisation process. They said the value of vouchers issued significantly exceeds the value of companies currently available.
- Brokers at the Slovenian stock exchange said they expected the number of foreign investors in Slovenia's securities to increase significantly in the future.
- Petrol trading company is still awaiting the Privatisation Agency's confirmation of its privatisation process conducted last year.
